title: Go: Error Handling
description: Handle errors using the error interface, custom errors, fmt.Errorf with %w, and basic panic/recover.

steps.title: Error Interface
steps.description: Create an `error` value from `errors.New("something went wrong")` and print it.

verification.failureMessage: Create and print an error using errors.New.

steps.title: Returning Errors
steps.description: Write a function `divide(a, b int) (int, error)` that returns an error when dividing by zero, otherwise returns the quotient. Print the result.

verification.failureMessage: Return an error from divide(10, 0) and print it.

steps.title: fmt.Errorf with %w
steps.description: Use `fmt.Errorf` with `%w` to wrap an error. Create a base error "not found" and wrap it as "user not found". Print the wrapped error.
hints: `%w` creates a wrapped error for unwrapping later.

verification.failureMessage: Wrap 'not found' as 'user not found' using %w and print.

steps.title: Custom Error Type
steps.description: Define a custom struct `ValidationError` that implements the `error` interface, with an `Field` string field. Create one and print it.

verification.failureMessage: Create ValidationError for field 'email' and print it.

steps.title: Panic and Recover
steps.description: Write a function `safeDivide(a, b int) (result int)` that uses `defer` and `recover()` to handle a panic when dividing by zero, returning 0. Print the result.
hints: `defer func() { if r := recover(); r != nil { result = 0 } }()`
Named return `result` lets recover set it.

verification.failureMessage: Handle division by zero with panic/recover, return 0.
